items.q: Q1 · Does POC migration predict direction?
items.why: Yes, by a statistical hair: +0.019σ at 15 min [+0.010, +0.029], above all 20 placebos, positive in both halves. That is ≈0.5 NQ points per signal in 2020–25 against a 0.73-point round trip, and below the registered 0.05σ bar.

items.q: Q1 · Beyond the price move already made?
items.why: The same rule on box closes gets about half of it. The increment is +0.009σ [−0.000, +0.018], and the 0.03σ bar is ruled out. Mostly short-term momentum that value tracks.

items.q: Q2 · Do VAH and VAL migrating too help?
items.why: −0.0005σ [−0.002, +0.001]. With 1-minute profiles, VAH and VAL move with the POC in 99% of migration windows, so the extra condition changes nothing.
−0.002σ [−0.015, +0.011] on the OHLCV delta proxy. This tests a price-derived proxy, not real aggressor flow.
−0.002σ [−0.024, +0.019], with an MDE of 0.049 against a 0.03 bar. The proxy recovers r ≈ 0.10 of true absorption, so the real question needs tick data.

items.q: Q5 · Does the full combination beat migration alone?
items.why: −0.003σ [−0.037, +0.029] on 3,131 windows. Nothing points to an improvement.
0 of 24 pass. The busy models lose 0.05–0.09R per trade net (gross ≈ 0). Signal minus random entry is +0.00 to +0.03R, while costs take ≈0.1R.
Strongly by hindsight day type (trend +0.09σ, consolidating −0.04σ at 15 min), not by ex-ante volatility (+0.016 to +0.029σ, overlapping). The split cannot be traded in advance.
